# Week 44, 2026

2026-10-26 to 2026-11-01 (UTC)

*One sensor. Emulated services. Generated by script from captured data — no model wrote this text.*

## Summary

2,074 addresses reached the sensor this week, 2,074 of them for the first time. 50% got as far as running a command. This is the first week with a comparable snapshot, so nothing here is measured against a previous period. 17 separate addresses fetched payloads from the same host, `27[.]215[.]121[.]33`. Shared delivery infrastructure across unrelated addresses is the difference between a campaign and a coincidence, though one sensor cannot tell whether that is one operator or several using the same loader.

## Credentials

4,779 distinct pairs across 527,369 recorded attempts. The ten most common account for 37% of those — a small dictionary applied relentlessly.

| username | password | attempts |

| `guest` | `12345` | 51,141 |

| `root` | `xc3511` | 16,934 |

| `guest` | `guest` | 14,495 |
| `user` | `user` | 14,227 |

| `admin` | `1234` | 11,855 |
| `root` | `vizxv` | 11,740 |
| `root` | `54321` | 11,396 |
| `draytek` | `1234` | 10,527 |

Only pairs tried at least three times by two or more independent addresses are listed. A pair guessed by several unrelated bots is a botnet dictionary entry; a single sighting might be a real person's password typed at the wrong host.

Inferred from the credentials and request paths chosen, which only make sense against those device families. It describes what the attacker was hunting, not anything about this machine.

## Method and caveats

- One sensor, one location. Absence from this dataset means only that this decoy did not see it.
- Services are emulated. Nothing was compromised, nothing was blocked, and no attack succeeded against real infrastructure.
- An address is recorded as observed. NAT and shared hosting mean one address may represent more than one device or person.
- Country data places the connecting device — usually a compromised consumer router — and is not attribution.
- Payload hosts are defanged here and are usually themselves compromised third parties.
- Nothing the sensor said in reply is published, here or anywhere: a transcript of the emulation's responses would let anyone build a detector for it.

Indicators, samples and per-address write-ups: https://github.com/1Birdo/lyrebird-intel
